title: Towards a Vibrant and Sustainable Creative Economy for the Arts
what_it_is: Towards a Vibrant and Sustainable Creative Economy for the Arts

sections.label: Creative economy in NAC Arts Plan
sections.summary: The creative economy was one of the key pillars in the NAC Arts Plan issued in September this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The creative economy was one of the key pillars in the latest National Arts Council (NAC) Arts Plan, which was issued in September this year.

sections.label: Funding to the sector
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2021, about $3.16 billion was provided to the sector as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2021, a total of approximately $3.16 billion had been provided to the sector as a whole.

sections.label: Creative UK case study
sections.summary: The Government may consider Creative UK, an independent network partly funded by The National Lottery, which set up a Creative Growth Finance fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government may wish to consider the case study of Creative UK.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is an independent network for the United Kingdom's (UK) Creative Industries, which is partly funded by The National Lottery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It has set up a Creative Growth Finance fund, which provides scale-up financing for promising for-profit creative businesses in the country.

sections.label: NAFA matched funding support
sections.summary: NAFA, an Institution of Public Character, does not benefit from the typical matched funding support MOE provides to IHLs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite being an Institution of Public Character, NAFA does not benefit from the typical matched funding support provided by the Ministry of Education (MOE) to Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs), and these include Institutes of Technical Education (ITE), polytechnics and autonomous universities.

sections.label: CMF matching grant conditions
sections.summary: CMF matching grants above the first S$300,000 per application window are now assessed on a project-by-project basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst other conditions, CMF matching grants above the first S$300,000 per application window are now assessed on a project-by-project basis.

sections.label: Fundraising benefits for new UAS
sections.summary: The Government is urged to ensure the new UAS and its member institutions enjoy the same fundraising benefits as other young universities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to urge the Government to ensure that our new UAS as well as its member institutions are able to enjoy the same fundraising benefits as our other young universities in the country.

sections.label: Global art market sales
sections.summary: The Art Basel and UBS Survey of Global Collecting in 2023 states global art market sales reached an estimated US$67.8 billion in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Art Basel and UBS Survey of Global Collecting in 2023 states that art market sales, globally, reached an estimated US$67.8 billion in 2022.

sections.label: Tax deductions for art donations
sections.summary: The Government offers a 250% tax deduction for donations to Institutions of Public Character, extended to 2026, and a Member asks for more dynamic incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Presently, the Government offers a 250% tax deduction for donations made to Institutions of Public Character, and these include many art charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is extremely commendable and it is heartening that the incentive has been extended to 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I would ask the Government to consider whether more dynamic incentives could be introduced, potentially those which can have more of a direct impact on working artists and on art consumption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In France, for example, a deduction is offered to taxpayers who purchase pieces of art made by living artists, provided that the artworks remain on display to the public or in places accessible to employees.

sections.label: Family income and creative professionals
sections.summary: The study found that for every $10,000 in additional family income, a person would be around 2% more likely to become a creative professional.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The study compared the socioeconomic backgrounds of artists and other creative professionals and found that, for every $10,000 in additional family income, a person would be around 2% more likely to become a creative professional.

sections.label: Supporting non-mainstream creative spaces
sections.summary: The Member hopes support is given to creatively rich spaces outside the mainstream and makes a case to give money to the arts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Entities like these do the hard work of developing young talents and more offbeat art offerings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is my hope that in our pursuit of a vibrant and sustainable creative economy, we do not forget to support – financially, if necessary – creatively rich spaces like these which sit outside of the mainstream.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A vibrant creative economy is one that is not just lucrative for its workers but also one which retains its diversity, its heart and its soul.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To conclude, I would like to return to Mr Tang Da Wu's somewhat biting exhortation for Singaporeans to not give money to the arts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope I have been able to make a case today for us to not only give money to the arts, but to work towards developing a viable and sustainable ecosystem for artists and creative producers to flourish and thrive.

sections.label: Support for self-employed arts workers
sections.summary: As nearly one-third of the arts workforce is self-employed, support has been ramped up to enhance career pathways and progression of self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As nearly one-third of the arts workforce is self-employed, we have ramped up our support to enhance career pathways and progression of self-employed persons (SEPs).

sections.label: Arts SEPs subscribed to ARH
sections.summary: More than 2,800 arts self-employed persons have already subscribed to ARH to benefit from its spaces and programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: More than 2,800 arts SEPs have already subscribed to ARH to benefit from its spaces and programmes.

sections.label: Skills Framework for the Arts
sections.summary: In September 2023, NAC and SkillsFuture Singapore developed the Skills Framework for the Arts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Most recently, in September 2023, the NAC and SkillsFuture Singapore developed the Skills Framework for the Arts.

sections.label: NAC grant support 2019-2023
sections.summary: From 2019 to 2023, NAC supported the sector with nearly $100 million in various grant support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: From 2019 to 2023, NAC supported the sector with nearly $100 million in various grant support.

sections.label: stART fund private sector support
sections.summary: Introduced in 2021, the stART fund has disbursed over $1 million from the private sector to 31 arts organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2021, we introduced the stART fund to catalyse support for developing organisational capabilities and programmes in smaller arts organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since then, more than $1 million from the private sector has been disbursed to 31 arts organisations.

sections.label: Commitment to develop arts workforce
sections.summary: MCCY and NAC will continue to develop the arts workforce, create diversified spaces, provide funding and grow audiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Our arts and culture landscape has really come a long way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We will continue to strive and make strides to develop our arts workforce, create diversified spaces for the arts, provide funding support and grow discerning audiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Together with my colleagues at MCCY and NAC, we are committed to ensuring that the arts thrive and blossom in Singapore.

sections.label: Growing a vibrant arts ecosystem
sections.summary: The passage calls for growing a vibrant arts and culture ecosystem to enhance the creative economy and shared identity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Together, let us grow a vibrant arts and culture ecosystem to enhance our creative economy, deepen our shared identity and make Singapore a distinctive city and home we love.
